A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoLoRA research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, algorithms, tables and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST experiments, RoBERTa-Large GLUE evaluations, and Llama-2-7B commonsense, HumanEval and MMLU results in Sections 5–6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, ablations, heterogeneity experiments and resource measurements in Section 5 and Appendix A5.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same alternating updates and aggregation of LoRA matrices A and B. Algorithms 1 and 2 are unchanged apart from formatting and relocation to Appendix A1. The new freezing schedules and linear-network controls are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both retain MNIST, the same five GLUE tasks, eight commonsense tasks, and CodeAlpaca/Alpaca with HumanEval/MMLU evaluation. The added Dirichlet partitions, client counts and model controls change experimental settings within this coverage rather than introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 newly evaluates FLoRA, previously only cited, against RoLoRA on MNLI, QQP and QNLI at three client counts in Table 8, and includes it in Table 15's resource comparison. The existing comparators remain. FlexLoRA is not newly introduced: its v1 Appendix Table 6 results move into v3 Table 1.

E3.justification: v3 adds Dirichlet(0.5) partitions with 10 clients and Dirichlet(1.0) partitions with 15 clients, extends rank-2 evaluation to larger client counts, and adds 100-round convergence comparisons. It also introduces per-round communication and server-aggregation-time measurements. The original model sizes, learning-rate search and core hyperparameter tables are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test when learning A matters through switching between RoLoRA and FFA-LoRA (Figure 5), the effect of removing ReLU (Figure 6), and convergence beyond the original training budget (Figure 7). Dirichlet-partition tests add heterogeneity analysis. The existing equal-communication-budget analysis is retained as Figure 11, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: The new aggregation-time experiment explicitly reports averaging over 30 runs. Existing three-trial commonsense and five-seed HumanEval/MMLU mean-and-standard-deviation reporting is retained. Neither PDF comparison establishes an increase in repetitions for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: The retained GLUE, commonsense, HumanEval and MMLU table values are unchanged. v3 adds Dirichlet accuracies, high-client-count rank-2 results, FLoRA comparisons, diagnostic curves and resource measurements. For example, Table 15 newly reports aggregation times of 0.0182 seconds for RoLoRA and 0.0415 seconds for LoRA. These are added results, not improvements over earlier same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The rank-1 linear convergence results and FFA-LoRA loss analysis are largely retained. v3 adds Appendix A4, with bounded-gradient, smoothness and adapter-alignment assumptions, Theorem A4.4 and its derivation claiming O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence to stationarity. This substantially expands the mathematical scope beyond the earlier linear analysis.

C1.justification: v1's theoretical contribution centers on convergence in a tractable rank-1 linear setting. v3's abstract and contribution statement additionally claim a convergence proof under general smooth nonconvex conditions, promoted through Section 4.3. This broadens a central scientific claim; the alternating-optimization and empirical-robustness contributions otherwise remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A2 newly identifies limitations of the linear down-projection analysis and the assumption of full client participation. Appendix A5.3 distinguishes fixed-budget comparisons from full convergence and acknowledges FLoRA reaching 83.3% MNLI accuracy after 4000 rounds. New interpretations discuss learning A early and exploiting ReLU's expressiveness.

D1.justification: v3 adds definitions of the communication and aggregation-time measurements and a checklist statement that code was uploaded, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit GLUE validation/test-split description and commonsense training-data merging instructions. These documentation changes do not establish changes to the underlying retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through Appendix A2's comparisons with matrix sensing, federated matrix factorization, FedRep and personalized federated learning. It acknowledges concurrent LoRA-A2's similar alternating optimization, adds FedIT attribution, and discusses FedSA-LoRA's relationship to the new convergence analysis. These are substantive additions beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: v3 merges related work and preliminaries, moves both algorithms and the equal-communication-budget discussion into the appendix, and shortens repetitive linear-proof exposition. It rewrites the abstract, contribution statement and conclusion, reorganizes the appendices, and adds an appendix contents page and checklist. This materially changes the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redesigned with an additional performance panel; new ablation and convergence figures and comparison tables are added. The existing communication-budget plot moves to the appendix and changes panel arrangement, while retained tables receive revised formatting and highlighted RoLoRA rows.

improvement.justification: The added diagnostics, FLoRA comparisons, measured costs and explicit limitations strengthen support for the unchanged method. However, the new nonconvex guarantee has a substantive proof gap: in Appendix A4, equations 299–302 define D_A and D_B with terms linear in eta, so requiring D eta² >= D_A + D_B does not yield a vanishing D eta term or establish the claimed rate. Some reproducibility details are also removed. These material benefits and weaknesses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
